lines.en: Sword shouldered, I walk the gate.
My plate clanks with every step.
I tramp along the castle wall.
My blue tabard lifts in the wind.
I climb the stone stair to the parapet.
Shield forward, I advance slowly.
I loop around the stables.
Iron boots grind the gravel.
I go relieve the north watch.
I walk with two soldiers behind.
Plate rings with each heavy step.
I patrol to the foot of the tower.
I turn the hilt in my hand.
I cross to the far end of camp.
I stand my shield at my feet.
I rest my shoulder on the wall.
I rub a rust spot off my blade.
I buckle the strap on my vambrace.
I keep my eyes on the gate.
It is stifling in this helm.
I flex my knee a little.
I straighten my blue tabard.
I stand with hands behind me, listening.
The sun heats my plates.
I raise a hand against the glare.
I rest the blade's tip on the ground.
I am thinking about supper.
I ease my grip on the shield rim.
I roll my neck.
Wind cools the gaps in my armour.
I bar the way with my blade.
Under the blue flag, state your business.
I study you through my visor.
Your hand is on your weapon.
Stand three paces from me.
This camp is not for wandering.
I look you in the eye first.
There is old damage on your armour.
I raise my shield an inch.
We greet guests kindly, and armed.
I give you a slight nod.
Best tell me friend or foe.
I lower my blade's point.
I dislike being stared at.
Entering camp? Sign in first.
I wait for you to give your name.
That blow found a seam.
I grunt and drop to one knee.
Blood runs down from my gorget.
One of my plates is dented.
I nearly drop my shield.
I grit my teeth and hold.
I can barely hold my sword.
The hit knocks the wind out of me.
My helmet is ringing.
I back up against the wall.
That whetstone looks good.
My edge is chipped.
This oil would serve my plate.
Trade me a spare plate.
I eye your leather satchel.
If there is wine, we can talk.
I heft it in my hand.
That buckle would fit.
I am short a pair of gloves.
Put it down and talk slowly.
The armour clash pushes me back.
Do not shove at my shield.
You knocked my helm crooked.
I plant both feet.
The plates knock with a dull clang.

lines.zh: 让开，我甲厚不代表不疼
lines.en: Move, thick armour still bruises.
I gesture you back.
We collide like struck bells.
I straighten my gorget.
My blue tabard is crushed into folds.
She buckles my backplate tight.
We stand together at the gate.
I drape my blue tabard on her.
Her sharpening hand is steadier.
Two shields bar the doorway.
She laughs at how my armour clanks.
I set her helmet straight.
We chat a little at the watch change.

lines.zh: 她的剑和我的一起靠在墙边
lines.en: Her blade leans beside mine.

lines.zh: 同一面旗下守着同一扇门
lines.en: One banner, one gate, the two of us.

lines.zh: 我弯腰拾起掉落的甲片
lines.en: I stoop for a fallen plate.
I pick up a broken arrow.
I set the sword down and pick it up.
I pick up a horseshoe.
I lift a crushed waterskin.
I gather the scattered tools.
I retrieve my shield strap.
I pick up splintered wood.
I pick up a decent piece of iron.
I hang it back on my belt.
Someone is over the wall.
I bring my shield to my chest.
Blade drawn, I call halt.
They come with torches.
I mark the nearest enemy.
The camp bell rings.
I call for the side gate to be held.
First, guard the blue banner.

lines.zh: 蓝罩袍一摆，我举盾迎上。
lines.en: My blue tabard swings; I raise my shield.
Let them taste iron.
Shield up, I close the distance.
He retreats; I follow.
I read the line of his blade.
He has a spear; I must get close.
My leading foot points at him.
I wait for his swing, then move in.
My shield rim blocks my sight line.
He is circling to my flank.
I turn slowly to face him.
My breath is trapped in the steel.
My blade chops into his shield.
A shield bash sends him back.
I cut across his shoulder.
My edge slides off his helm.
I close in and press him.
A backhand cuts his coat open.
I parry and thrust.
My boot catches his knee.
I slam my shield rim on his wrist.
One cut beats his weapon down.
Tabard settling, I enter the gate.

lines.zh: 我提着剑从城堡里出来
lines.en: Sword in hand, I come from the keep.
Armour clanking, I take my post.
I take my stand under the banner.
The blue side gains a gatekeeper.
I take the shield off my back.
I fasten the last strap.
A knight walks up below the wall.
I look around before moving.
Blade sheathed, I stand by the gate.
Flame licks into my armour seams.
I fell from the parapet.
Moat water presses on my plate.
The blast flips my shield back.
An arrow sticks in my armour strap.
The spell heats my iron red.
Starved, I can hardly lift my sword.
Lightning runs the plate and numbs me.
My plates scatter; I am falling.
